resources.title: Cubers Megasurvey - Learning from ourselves (r/Cubers 6th Megasurvey, 2022 data, published Apr 2023)
resources.author: Basilio Noris (b4silio), with the r/Cubers mods; reviewed by Shawn Boucke (SpeedCubeReview)
resources.summary: A general cubing survey write-up: about 1,410 respondents, 160+ questions, a 92-page Keynote PDF and a cleaned raw .xlsx (991 columns). It is not a trainer, but it has real Roux-specific sections. rouxcubing.com cites it for 'Roux is about 6% of cubers'. Roux numbers from the PDF charts and my own pass over the raw data (49 respondents named Roux as their main method; small sample): (1) Median 3x3 global average by main method: Roux 16.49 vs CFOP 16.50, ZZ 12.50. Page title: 'Roux is faster than CFOP but it takes longer to master it'. Roux medians by experience run 38.7 (under 3 months), 32.5 (about 6 months), 25.3 (1 year), 14.5 (1.5 years), 13.2 (3 years). CFOP runs 38.3, 22.5, 17.8, 17.3, 14.3, so 'the learning curve is harsher for Roux'. (2) OH, from the raw data: Roux mains median OH 20.4 (n=20) vs CFOP 31.2 (n=232). 45% of Roux mains practise OH, against 28% of all respondents. (3) Roux orientation neutrality: Fixed (y or y2) 21%, Dual (x2 y) 57%, Full (x y) 14%, Reduced (x2 y2) 4%, Quad 3%. Median averages by neutrality: Full 14.5, Fixed 14.3, Dual 14.0, Quad 13.9, Reduced 12.1. The overall conclusion: dual colour neutrality learns fastest. (4) Roux inspection planning ('Always' / 'Mostly' / 'Only if easy'): FS or line 65/23/13%; full FB 16/37/47%; FB+SS 91% and FB+SB 93% 'only if easy'. 70% of fast learners do not use a strict 15 s inspection. (5) 18 of the 21 Meyer 4x4 users are Roux mains. Among Roux mains, 4x4 methods are Meyer 18, Yau 15, Reduction 10, K4 5, Hoya 4. (6) Learning: 43 of 49 Roux mains know full CMLL. Roux mains use on-device alg sheets 40/49, sheets by others 28, an alg trainer 26, YouTube 19, their own sheets 15, a smart cube with a trainer 6. Bulk 'whole set over several days' (14) beats '1-2 algs a day' (7). (7) Smart cubes (all respondents): 33% own one, 17% stopped using it. Main uses: solve analysis and splits 79% (up from 67%), online competing 51%, alg trainers 37%. Drawbacks: cube performance 55%, having to use an app 50%, battery 46%, connection 43%, weight 37%. The author's note: 'Dear smart cube software developers, please put more effort in your analytics!' (8) Timers: csTimer 58% and Twisty Timer (Android) 17%; among Roux mains csTimer 38/44 and Twisty Timer 9. (9) Roux Weekly Comp on Facebook: 3% of respondents and 12 of 49 Roux mains. Also saved: the PDF text (megasurvey6-pdf.txt), my Roux analysis (megasurvey6-roux-analysis.txt) and the PDF/xlsx with page renders (megasurvey6-files/). No later edition is hosted (megasurvey7 returns 404). The Wayback Machine was not used.
drills: None directly. Implied: an inspection-planning progression from FS/line to full FB to FB+SS (most Roux mains always plan FS, but only 16% always plan the full FB)
Implied: colour or orientation-neutrality practice (x2 y dual is the norm and learns fastest)
Implied: OH Roux practice (Roux mains' OH median is about 11 s faster than CFOP mains')
Implied: bulk alg-set learning repeated over several days vs 1-2 algs a day (both styles are common)
infoTopics: Is Roux competitive: Roux vs CFOP vs ZZ medians, and Roux's harsher first-year learning curve
Roux share of the community (about 6% main; 47% of respondents know Roux)
Roux orientation-neutrality options (fixed, dual x2y, reduced x2y2, full xy, quad) and their speeds
How far Roux solvers plan in inspection
How cubers learn algs (tools, bulk vs incremental)
What cubers want from smart cubes (analytics) and what bothers them
Which timers cubers use (csTimer, Twisty Timer)

Solve-time distribution histogram, like Basilio's 'Fancy Charts' generator on basilio.dev/cubing
Give big-cube Roux (Meyer) priority: most Meyer users are Roux mains

resources.title: SpeedCubeShop sponsor link for the Roux Weekly Competition
resources.author: SpeedCubeShop (commercial store)
resources.summary: Sponsor link from the Weekly Competition #607 post ('Sponsored by SpeedCubeShop ... Use code ROUX for 5% off'; one random competitor each week wins a $5 SCS gift card). The link resolves, but the target page is gone. Redirect chain: speedcubeshop.com/rouxcomp → www.speedcubeshop.com/pages/roux?utm_source=weekly_roux&utm_medium=community_sponsorship&utm_campaign=weekly_roux → speedcubeshop.com/pages/roux → www.speedcubeshop.com/ → speedcubeshop.com/. So the /pages/roux landing page no longer exists, and the link lands on the store homepage, which has no Roux-specific content. The Wayback Machine was not reachable (archive.org returned 429; web.archive.org was blocked by egress policy; not routed around). No training or informational value. It only matters as a pattern: a cube store sponsors a Roux community event with a discount code and a prize draw. Homepage text is saved in speedcubeshop-rouxcomp.txt.
appIdeas: Possible funding route for the owner's donations/IAP question: an optional, clearly labelled 'Support / Gear' link or sponsor credit (store discount code) kept out of training screens. The Roux weekly comp already runs on this model. Product listings are not Roux content, so keep them out of the app

resources.title: Winning Roux weekly FMC solution (Anomic, 43 moves STM) on alg.cubing.net
resources.author: Anomic (competitor); hosted on alg.cubing.net (Lucas Garron)
resources.summary: A bit.ly link to an alg.cubing.net reconstruction: last week's (#606) winning Roux FMC solution. Setup: R' U' F B2 D' L2 D2 F2 L2 F2 U R2 D B2 L D F' D U' R2 B2 F' R' F2 R' U' F. Solution, with step comments: y x' // inspection | R' r' D2 R U' R2 D' // FB (7) | U' R' U2 R' U' R' U M2 U' r' U r // SB (12) | F R' F' R U2 R U' R' U R U2' R' // CMLL (12) | U2 M U M' U' M2 U' M' U2 M2 U2 M' // LSE (12). I verified it with the cubing.js 0.52.4 KPuzzle: it solves the scramble, 7+12+12+12 = 43 STM. alg.cubing.net reports 50 HTM, 64 QTM, 43 STM and 45 ETM (7 slice moves), so under WCA counting it would be 50. The CMLL is onionhoney's 'pi_back_slash' alg without its leading U (src/lib/Algs.tsx:36). LSE is 12 moves of pure <M,U>. Useful as a reference for per-step Roux efficiency and for the alg.cubing.net URL format: setup= and alg= params, '_' for space, '-' for prime, %0A for newline, // comments. alg.cubing.net is frozen; its successor is Twizzle (alpha.twizzle.net/edit, part of cubing.js).
drills: Linear Roux efficiency: FB in about 7, SB in about 12, CMLL about 12, LSE about 12 STM (one winning data point)
Study the reconstruction: inspection rotation choice (y x'), FB with r/D moves, SB finished with an M2 and r' U r insert
